sentiment: We grow blind to what we know by heart, while quiet inventions chill the world without a sound.

stories.title: Bug Blindness
stories.summary: The longer we live with a system, the less we see its flaws — expertise quietly builds its own blind spots, and the familiar becomes invisible.

stories.title: Benjamin Franklin's Alter Egos Gave Him the Most Freedom
stories.summary: Speaking through another name let Franklin say what he could not as himself — a change of frame is a kind of liberty.

stories.title: The Einstein-Szilard Refrigerator
stories.summary: A brilliant machine with no moving parts — the deepest elegance is what works silently, without noise, until you stop to look.
